newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent trades diverge as paper spreads climb.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent trades diverge as paper spreads climb.

text.p: Dated Brent traded at widely divergent prices on Thursday and life returned to the markets in other North Sea grades after most of September's loading programmes were released, traders said.
Dated Brent loading August 28-30 and August 27-29 traded at September -5 and -7 cts respectively, a leap above the -12 cents paid the previous day.
Some traders argued the deals were not justified by market fundamentals and were done to benefit long CFD positions.

Others said the trading house that bought both cargoes from a British major was short to a U.S. refiner and had been defeated in his attempts to keep the cargoes from the paper chains on previous days.
A European major later paid a trading house 29 cents below September for a prompt August 20-22 loader and argued that level was closer to the reality of the market.
"The Brent is break-even on what we could do on other grades," the buyer said.
The cash Brent market firmed throughout the day on the back of the early physical deals and ahead of the expiry of the September IPE contract, which was up 16 cents at $19.14 a barrel by 1745 gmt.
The Sept/Oct intermonth spread fetched a confirmed -2 cents and was rumoured sold at parity, with Oct/Nov also trading stronger at -10 and -8 cents.
Short-term swaps also got a lift from the Brent deals. Next week (Aug 18-22) traded earlier at October Brent -25 and -23 cents before jumping 10 cents in value to be offered around -12 cents.
The subsequent week (Aug 25-29) also gained some 15 cents on the day to go out valued at -0.17/-0.13 below October Brent.
With the major British and Norwegian loading programmes released on Thursday the brakes came off the market in non-Brent North Sea crude, with deals done at largely steady numbers.

An August 26-28 Forties traded at a steady dated Brent +31 cents, an end-month Oseberg at a cheapish +15 cents and a Draugen for Sept 4-6 at dated plus 35 cents. A Statfjord and an Ekofisk traded on a private and confidential basis.

The market derived some early support from the Brent and Forties programmes, which came in thinner than expected, with Brent down three full cargoes on August and Forties 2.68 million barrels lighter.
The Oseberg loading schedule was some two million barrels heavier than the previous month, while Gullfaks was down some nine 855,000 barrel cargoes because of scheduled maintenance.

The future complexion of the Mediterranean sour market was beginning to change on Thursday as the first Iraqi barrels since May began to load from the Turkish port of Ceyhan, bound for the U.S. aboard the Bayoil chartered VLCC Arcadia.
But some life remained in the Urals market, with traders insisting that prompt barrels were better valued than the -90 cents, basis cif Augusta, currently being talked.
One Med trader was reported to have sold his August 18-20 loading Urals to another trader at a number "in the very low 70s."
Kirkuk barrels were being actively offered, but with no takers yet, and reports that the premium demanded over official selling price had dropped from 20 cents to 10-15 cents.
In North West Europe Urals deals were rumoured at 95 cents below dated Brent but could not be confirmed.
-- Sean Maguire, London newsroom +44 171 542 8060
